title: Dewey Fig. 8: single human ear, distortion component (all 386 clean observed points)
attribution: James B. Dewey, Sources of microstructure in mammalian cochlear responses, JARO (2025); source measurements described in Dewey and Dhar (2017).
limitations: The source identifies one human ear but provides no subject identifier or ear-specific audiogram in this artifact. Hearing health is not reported; these data are not eligible as verified normal-hearing ground truth.
The values are the separated dpoae_D distortion component, not the total DPOAE or the reflection component. A model without reflection cannot be judged against full fine structure using this curve.

The measurements used logarithmically swept primaries and frequency-domain/time-window component separation. Discrete steady two-tone simulations are an approximation, not a matched reproduction of the acquisition or analysis.
The measured input levels are L1=51 and L2=36 dB FPL. Treating those numbers as nominal dB SPL is not an FPL-to-SPL conversion or matched calibration.
Levels are measured dB SPL at the ear canal. Uncalibrated model units support relative amplitude shape comparison only, not absolute SPL error or pass/fail validation.
Phase values are retained exactly in source cycles; the artifact does not specify an absolute phase-reference convention. No absolute-phase agreement or literal propagation delay is implied.

All points with finite dp_f, mag_clean, and phi_clean are retained in source order. The author describes clean fields as responses greater than 6 dB above the measurement noise floor. This extraction uses the supplied clean mask, without recomputing SNR; no noise-floor vector is supplied in dpoae_D. These are single-ear component estimates, not a population reference range.
The published Fig. 8 plot zooms to approximately 2.9–5.1 kHz DP frequency. This dataset retains the full clean dpoae_D vector stored in fig8.mat rather than only the displayed zoom.

The distributed artifact contains processed component estimates; observation here means an existing tabulated source estimate, not an unprocessed microphone sample. No interpolation of measured level or phase is performed by this extraction.

provenance.eligibility: finite(dp_f) and finite(mag_clean) and finite(phi_clean), preserving source order
provenance.selection: All eligible observations. No downsampling, interpolation, smoothing, phase wrapping, phase unwrapping, or replacement is performed by this extraction.
provenance.frequency_derivation: f1_hz = dp_hz / (2 - ratio); f2_hz = ratio * f1_hz. Source dpoae_D has dp_f, not f2_f.

source_protocol.component_separation: inverse FFT with frequency windows and time-domain component windows; see methods DOI

provenance.source_index_convention: Zero-based index into the 454-element fig8.dpoae_D vectors; MATLAB index = source_index_zero_based + 1.
